alerts.title: ★★★★★ Section: Manhattan skyline behind you
alerts.text: You're out of the Hudson tunnel and crossing the Meadowlands marshes. Look back to the LEFT for the Manhattan skyline, including the Empire State Building and One World Trade Center.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Portal Bridge (Hackensack River)
alerts.text: The train crosses the Hackensack River, where the old 1910 Portal swing bridge is being replaced by the new Portal North Bridge.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Passaic River & Newark Penn
alerts.text: The train crosses the Passaic River on the Dock Bridge lift span, then stops at Newark Penn Station.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Newark Airport
alerts.text: Look LEFT for Newark Liberty Airport, with jets taking off and landing and the AirTrain monorail.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Raritan River & New Brunswick
alerts.text: The train crosses the Raritan River on a long bridge into New Brunswick, home of Rutgers. Look down the river.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ Princeton Junction
alerts.text: Princeton Junction, where the little two-mile 'Dinky' shuttle branches off to Princeton University.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ Trenton
alerts.text: This is Trenton, New Jersey's capital. The gold State House dome may show RIGHT. The Delaware River crossing is right after the station.

alerts.title: ★★★★☆ Delaware River: 'Trenton Makes'
alerts.text: The train crosses the Delaware into Pennsylvania. Look RIGHT for the 'TRENTON MAKES THE WORLD TAKES' sign on the road bridge next to you.

alerts.title: ★★★★☆ Schuylkill River crossing
alerts.text: The train crosses the Schuylkill River and runs down its bank to 30th Street. Look downriver (LEFT) toward Boathouse Row, the Art Museum and the Center City skyline.

alerts.title: ★★★★☆ 30th Street Station
alerts.text: This is Philadelphia's grand 1933 30th Street Station. The train reverses here during a long stop, then heads west out the Main Line.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Section: Philadelphia Main Line
alerts.text: Past Overbrook the train runs out the historic Main Line, past leafy suburbs, stone stations and college towns, to Paoli.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ Bryn Mawr
alerts.text: This is a classic Main Line stone station and suburb. Haverford and Villanova are just down and up the line.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Coatesville: Brandywine & steel mill
alerts.text: The line crosses high over the West Branch Brandywine. Look down at the long steel mill that grew from Lukens Steel, one of America's oldest.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ Parkesburg
alerts.text: Chester County's hills and old iron towns give way to Lancaster County farm country ahead.

alerts.title: ★★★★☆ Section: Amish farmland
alerts.text: At Gap the line drops into Lancaster County farm country. Watch for Amish farms, horse-drawn buggies, big barns and windmills from here to Lancaster.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Leaman Place
alerts.text: This is the junction for the Strasburg Rail Road, a steam tourist line. Farmland continues on both sides.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Farmland: buggies & barns
alerts.text: Keep watching the back roads for horse-drawn buggies and the farms' big barns. Lancaster is a few minutes ahead.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Lancaster
alerts.text: This is Lancaster's grand 1929 station. After Elizabethtown the line follows the Susquehanna valley to Harrisburg.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Three Mile Island
alerts.text: Look LEFT across the fields and river for the Three Mile Island cooling towers. They may show through gaps in the trees.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Harrisburg
alerts.text: Harrisburg: the train swaps its electric locomotive for a diesel here, so expect a longer stop. Look LEFT for the Capitol dome as you arrive. Rockville Bridge comes soon after.

alerts.title: ★★★★☆ Section: Susquehanna River
alerts.text: The line follows the wide Susquehanna north from Harrisburg. Two top sights come next: the Rockville Bridge, then the Statue of Liberty out in the river.

alerts.title: ★★★★★ Rockville Bridge
alerts.text: The train crosses the Rockville Bridge (1902), the world's longest stone-arch railroad bridge, with 48 arches. Look upstream (RIGHT) toward the mountain gap.

alerts.title: ★★★★★ Statue of Liberty (Dauphin Narrows)
alerts.text: Look RIGHT, out in the river: a 25-ft Statue of Liberty replica stands on an old bridge pier in the Susquehanna.

alerts.title: ★★★★☆ Section: Juniata River
alerts.text: At Duncannon the line leaves the Susquehanna and turns up the Juniata. The Appalachian Trail crosses here on the Clarks Ferry Bridge. River and ridges all the way to Lewistown.

alerts.title: ★★★★☆ Section: Lewistown Narrows
alerts.text: In the Lewistown Narrows, the Juniata squeezes between the steep Blue and Shade Mountain ridges. Keep watching for the next ~10 miles.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Lewistown Narrows: Denholm bend
alerts.text: Watch the big river bend with the ridges around it. Remains of the old canal corridor are across the river.

alerts.title: ★★★★☆ Lewistown Narrows: Hawstone
alerts.text: You're deep in the narrows at Hawstone, where the river, highway and railroad share the gorge.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ End of the narrows
alerts.text: The narrows open out toward Lewistown. Its 1849 depot is just ahead.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Lewistown: 1849 depot
alerts.text: Watch for the historic 1849 depot at Lewistown, one of the oldest surviving Pennsylvania Railroad stations. Jacks Narrows comes after Mount Union.

alerts.title: ★★★★☆ Section: Jacks Narrows
alerts.text: At Mount Union the line enters Jacks Narrows, a water gap through Jacks Mountain. Watch the river and the mountain walls closing in.

alerts.title: ★★★★☆ Jacks Narrows: Thousand Steps
alerts.text: Look RIGHT up the steep quarried face of Jacks Mountain. The Thousand Steps, built by quarry workers, climb it, though trees can hide them.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ Mapleton: end of the narrows
alerts.text: This is the west end of Jacks Narrows at Mapleton. Huntingdon is next.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ Huntingdon
alerts.text: Huntingdon station and riverside town. The Little Juniata gorge starts at Petersburg, about 10 minutes ahead.

alerts.title: ★★★★☆ Section: Little Juniata gorge
alerts.text: From Petersburg the line winds up the Little Juniata gorge, with repeated river crossings, close wooded ridges and a tunnel. It's scenic all the way to Tyrone.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Little Juniata: Barree
alerts.text: Big river bends and steep wooded slopes around Barree.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Spruce Creek tunnel
alerts.text: The line tunnels through a spur of Tussey Mountain here. GPS may drop out briefly.

alerts.title: ★★★★☆ Little Juniata: river crossings
alerts.text: This is a run of crossings over the Little Juniata. Look down at the river and at the stone-arch bridge piers.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Little Juniata: Birmingham
alerts.text: Watch the river crossings and folded ridges around Birmingham.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ Tyrone: top of the gorge
alerts.text: Tyrone station, at the head of the Little Juniata gorge. Altoona's rail yards come next, then Horseshoe Curve.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ East Altoona yards
alerts.text: The Altoona rail yards start here. The Juniata locomotive shops are next.

alerts.title: ★★★★☆ Juniata locomotive shops
alerts.text: Look RIGHT for the giant Juniata shops, among the largest locomotive repair shops in North America. You may spot locomotives parked outside.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Altoona: station & railroad museum
alerts.text: Altoona station. The Railroaders Memorial Museum is beside the tracks on the LEFT. After the stop the train climbs to Horseshoe Curve.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Section: climb to Horseshoe Curve
alerts.text: Leaving Altoona, the line starts its climb up the Allegheny Front. Horseshoe Curve is a few miles ahead.

alerts.title: ★★★★★ Horseshoe Curve: get to a window
alerts.text: Horseshoe Curve is coming up on the climb. Get to a window now. On the bend you can often see the front or back of your own train.

alerts.title: ★★★★★ Horseshoe Curve
alerts.text: You're on the 1854 Horseshoe Curve now. Look LEFT, to the inside of the bend, for the park, the reservoirs below, and the rest of your train curving around.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Gallitzin: Allegheny Tunnel
alerts.text: You're near the summit at Gallitzin, with Gallitzin Tunnels Park beside the tracks. The Allegheny Tunnel (3,600 ft) is next; GPS cuts out inside.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ Cresson: over the summit
alerts.text: You're over the summit of the old Pennsylvania Railroad main line. The long descent to Johnstown begins.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Section: down the Little Conemaugh
alerts.text: The line descends along the Little Conemaugh River through Lilly, South Fork and Mineral Point to Johnstown, with wooded slopes closing in.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ South Fork: 1889 flood history
alerts.text: The South Fork Dam stood just up the valley from here. Its failure in 1889 sent the flood that destroyed Johnstown. The memorial site is out of view.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ Mineral Point
alerts.text: The valley narrows toward Johnstown. The 1889 flood ran down this same valley, following the river beside you.

alerts.title: ★★★★☆ Johnstown: Stone Bridge & Incline
alerts.text: Johnstown station. Right after it, the train crosses the 1888 Stone Bridge, where debris from the 1889 Johnstown Flood piled up. Look LEFT for the Inclined Plane climbing the steep hillside above the city.

alerts.title: ★★★★★ Section: Conemaugh Gap
alerts.text: West of Johnstown the line enters the Conemaugh Gap, the deep gorge the river carved through Laurel Ridge, well over 1,000 ft deep. Watch both sides for the next ~10 miles.

alerts.title: ★★★★★ Conemaugh Gap: heart of the gorge
alerts.text: You're in the deepest part of the gorge now. Look up at the ridgetops towering over the river.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Seward: out of the gorge
alerts.text: The gorge opens out at Seward. Chestnut Ridge and Packsaddle Gap come next.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ New Florence: between the ridges
alerts.text: This is an open valley between Laurel Ridge, behind you, and Chestnut Ridge, ahead.

alerts.title: ★★★★☆ Section: Packsaddle Gap
alerts.text: At Bolivar the line follows the Conemaugh River where it cuts through Chestnut Ridge. Watch the steep wooded walls rise on both sides. This is the last mountain gap.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ Derry
alerts.text: Derry is an old Pennsylvania Railroad yard town. The mountains are behind you now: rolling farmland to Latrobe and Greensburg.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ Latrobe
alerts.text: Latrobe is the hometown of Fred Rogers and Arnold Palmer, and where the banana split was invented.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Greensburg: courthouse dome
alerts.text: Look LEFT for the tall dome of the Westmoreland County Courthouse above town. Greensburg's restored 1912 station is next to the tracks.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ Jeannette, the Glass City
alerts.text: Jeannette grew around huge glass works. Look for old factory sites and the brick town beside the line.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ Section: Brush Creek valley
alerts.text: Past Manor the line descends the wooded Brush Creek valley toward Trafford, with small towns and hillside farms.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Section: Turtle Creek valley
alerts.text: Past Pitcairn the line follows Turtle Creek through the old Westinghouse company towns: the Air Brake 'Castle' at Wilmerding, then the huge George Westinghouse Bridge.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ Pitcairn yard
alerts.text: This is Norfolk Southern's Pitcairn yard. Look for long rows of freight cars, containers and locomotives.

alerts.title: ★★★☆☆ Wilmerding: the Westinghouse 'Castle'
alerts.text: Watch for the turreted brick Westinghouse Air Brake office building, the castle of this old company town, right by the tracks.

alerts.title: ★★★★☆ George Westinghouse Bridge
alerts.text: Look up: the 1932 concrete-arch bridge carrying US 30 soars high over the valley and the tracks.

alerts.title: ★★☆☆☆ Pittsburgh
alerts.text: End of the line: Pittsburgh. The station sits below the old 1903 Pennsylvania Railroad station, now The Pennsylvanian, with its domed rotunda out front.
